task_context.reference_solution:
From the angle addition formula,
\[1 = \tan 45^\circ = \tan (20^\circ + 25^\circ) = \frac{\tan 20^\circ + \tan 25^\circ}{1 - \tan 20^\circ \tan 25^\circ},\]so $\tan 20^\circ + \tan 25^\circ = 1 - \tan 20^\circ \tan 25^\circ.$

Then
\[(1 + \tan 20^\circ)(1 + \tan 25^\circ) = 1 + \tan 20^\circ + \tan 25^\circ + \tan 20^\circ \tan 25^\circ = \boxed{2}.\]

Okay, $20 + 25 = 45$. I know $\tan 45^\circ = 1$. How does that help me with $(1 + \tan 20^\circ)(1 + \tan 25^\circ)$?

Since $\tan(20^\circ + 25^\circ) = 1$, you can use the tangent addition formula: $\tan(A+B) = \frac{\tan A + \tan B}{1 - \tan A \tan B}$. Try setting this formula equal to 1 using $A=20^\circ$ and $B=25^\circ$ and see what relationship you can derive between $\tan 20^\circ$ and $\tan 25^\circ$.

So $1 = (\tan 20 + \tan 25) / (1 - \tan 20 \tan 25)$. That means $1 - \tan 20 \tan 25 = \tan 20 + \tan 25$. Now if I expand the original expression, I get $1 + \tan 20 + \tan 25 + \tan 20 \tan 25$. If I replace the $\tan 20 + \tan 25$ part with $1 - \tan 20 \tan 25$, everything cancels except for two 1s. So the answer is 2, right?
